DEC, IPHS, GENERIC, Ports, and Reaction Structure

Structural governance lifecycle

A constitutive rate formula specifies process speed under local conditions; structural governance additionally specifies discrete spatial support, conserved elemental ledgers, conjugate thermodynamic efforts, port power exchange, and overflow residual routing (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapters 8, 9, 12, and 13). In RELIC, Discrete Exterior Calculus (DEC), Irreversible Port-Hamiltonian System (IPHS), and General Equation for Non-Equilibrium Reversible-Irreversible Coupling (GENERIC) operators augment the single runtime lifecycle without introducing a second simulator, state manager, or registry:

\[ \text{Scientific ABC} \;\Longrightarrow\; \text{Canonical Bridge} \;\Longrightarrow\; \texttt{FunctorBase} \;\Longrightarrow\; \texttt{ParameterManager} + \texttt{StateManager} \;\Longrightarrow\; \text{DEC / IPHS / GraphIR Audit}. \]

Every Graph Intermediate Representation (GraphIR, relic.orchestration.graph_ir) compilation pass (compile_graph in relic.orchestration.compiler) emits a normalized 13-key report.audit summary (syntax_ok, semantic_ok, assertion_ok, assertion_audit, conservation_audit, port_matching_audit, overflow_routing_audit, equivalence_certificate_audit, reaction_network_audit, integration_plan_audit, global_compile_audit, validation_error_count, validation_warning_count). Software wiring nullspace vectors (topology_signature.conservation_vectors in relic.orchestration.topology_algebra) summarize topological incidence \(\ker(\mathbf{B}^{\mathsf{T}})\) and never substitute for physical mass or energy conservation committed through StateManager.

Discrete exterior calculus (relic.computation.operators.dec)

Ten-field typed cochain spaces (CochainSpaceSpec)

On an oriented cellular complex \(K\), a discrete \(k\)-form is a \(k\)-cochain \(\alpha^k \in C^k(K)\) (\(k = 0\) on vertices, \(1\) on oriented edges, \(2\) on faces, \(3\) on volumes). CochainSpaceSpec (relic.computation.operators.dec.forms) declares each finite-dimensional cochain space via ten frozen fields:

Field

Python type

Mathematical and structural role

complex_id

str

Identifier of the cellular complex \(K\)

degree

FormDegree (0, 1, 2, 3)

Cochain degree \(k\)

primality

Primality ("primal", "dual")

Primal complex \(K\) or dual complex \(K^\ast\) placement

n_dofs

int

Positive finite number of degrees of freedom (\(n > 0\))

units

str

Canonical physical unit of cochain pairings

extensivity

Extensivity ("intensive", "extensive", "density", "integral")

DEC cochain pairing semantics (distinct from SpatialQuantityBasis)

physical_domain

str

Governed physical or elemental domain label

semantic_name

str

Canonical variable or field semantic identifier

orientation_convention

str

Inner or outer orientation convention on \(K\) or \(K^\ast\)

boundary_role

BoundaryRole ("interior", "boundary", "port", "mixed")

Topological boundary participation role

Coboundary exactness and Stokes pairing

The discrete exterior derivative \(D_k: C^k(K) \rightarrow C^{k+1}(K)\) is the transpose of the chain boundary incidence matrix, \(D_k = \partial_{k+1}^{\mathsf{T}}\), satisfying the exact topological nilpotency identity (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapter 8):

\[ D_{k+1} D_k = 0, \qquad \langle D_k \alpha,\; c \rangle = \langle \alpha,\; \partial_{k+1} c \rangle. \]

cochain_complex_check (relic.validation.framework.rules.dec_complex) verifies \(D_{k+1} D_k = 0\) against validation.dec_complex.cochain_residual_tolerance (strict validation also requires integer incidence entries, \(D_0 \mathbf{1} = 0\), and boundary subcomplex closure). typed_stokes_audit (relic.computation.operators.dec.complex) evaluates the discrete Stokes pairing on supplied cochain/chain vectors as a finite point check.

Linear chain maps (LinearChainMap)

LinearChainMap (relic.computation.operators.dec.chain_map) represents a unit-aware linear operator \(M \in \mathbb{R}^{n_t \times n_s}\) between declared source and target CochainSpaceSpec spaces with positive unit-conversion factor \(u > 0\). Construction (__post_init__) enforces four fail-closed checks:

  1. Two-dimensional matrix rank: matrix.ndim == 2;

  2. Exact degree-of-freedom shape match: tuple(matrix.shape) == (target.n_dofs, source.n_dofs);

  3. Finite entries: torch.isfinite(matrix).all(); and

  4. Strictly positive unit scale: unit_factor > 0.0.

Application, composition, unit-adjusted ledger preservation (preserves_ledger against validation.iphs.chain_map_ledger_tolerance), perturbation error bounding (error_bound), and operator distance (distance, close_within) satisfy:

\[ y = u M x, \qquad \max_{i,j}\lvert \left(C_t (u M) - C_s\right)_{ij} \rvert \le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{cm}}, \qquad \lVert u M \delta x \rVert_2 \le \lVert u M \rVert_2\,\lVert \delta x \rVert_2, \]
\[ d(M_1, M_2) = \lVert u_1 M_1 - u_2 M_2 \rVert_2. \]

Exact equality equals (\(d = 0\) with identical spaces and unit_factor) is an equivalence relation; close_within (\(d(M_1, M_2) \le \varepsilon\)) is reflexive and symmetric without transitivity. Coboundary commutation \(P_{k+1} D_k^{(a)} = D_k^{(b)} P_k\) is audited separately by chain_map_check (relic.validation.framework.rules.chain_map).

Hodge star and constitutive metrics (HodgeStarSpec)

HodgeStarSpec (relic.computation.operators.dec.hodge) maps primal \(k\)-cochains to dual \((n - k)\)-cochains, \(\star_k: C^k(K) \rightarrow C^{n-k}(K^\ast)\), inducing the discrete inner product \(\langle \alpha, \beta \rangle_k = \alpha^{\mathsf{T}} H_k \beta\) via matrix \(H_k\) backed by ParameterManager parameter_keys and metric_keys. Calling HodgeStarSpec.validate() and hodge_psd_check (relic.validation.framework.rules.hodge) verifies compatible domain/codomain spaces, finite entries, and role-specific definiteness:

\[ H_k = H_k^{\mathsf{T}}, \qquad z^{\mathsf{T}} H_k z > 0 \quad \forall z \neq 0 \;\; (\text{metric SPD}), \qquad z^{\mathsf{T}} H_k z \ge 0 \;\text{with}\; H_k K = 0,\; \dim K = \operatorname{nullity}(H_k) \;\; (\text{material PSD}). \]

A singular material operator must supply its complete linearly independent kernel_basis \(K\) and never substitutes for an invertible metric Hodge star. With storage cochain \(x\) and flux cochain \(f\), semi-discrete conservative transport \(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = -D^{\mathsf{T}} f + s + b\) lowers into governed StateManager updates via typed_cochain_delta_to_update_item (relic.computation.operators.dec.adapters).

Irreversible port-Hamiltonian and GENERIC lowering

IPHSStructureSpec, PortSpecIPHS, assemble_iphs_structure, advance_reaction_network, and poisson_jacobi_residual (relic.computation.operators.iphs) separate dissipative port-Hamiltonian (dissipative_ph) realizations from GENERIC / metriplectic (generic) realizations without mixing energy resistance \(R_h\) and entropy mobility \(M_h\) (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapters 9, 12, and 13).

Dissipative port-Hamiltonian (dissipative_ph) realization

For storage functional \(H(x)\) with conjugate effort \(e_H = \nabla_x H(x)\), port input \(u_h\), port matrix \(G_h\), and conjugate output \(y_h = G_h^{\mathsf{T}} e_H\), the canonical dissipative_ph drift (M_h = 0) evaluated by IPHSStructureSpec.canonical_drift is:

\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = (J_h - R_h) e_H + G_h u_h + N_h r_h, \qquad J_h^{\mathsf{T}} = -J_h, \qquad R_h = R_h^{\mathsf{T}} \succeq 0. \]

Because \(e_H^{\mathsf{T}} J_h e_H = 0\), closed reaction-free trajectories satisfy \(\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}t} = -e_H^{\mathsf{T}} R_h e_H \le 0\), and open trajectories satisfy \(\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}t} = -e_H^{\mathsf{T}} R_h e_H + y_h^{\mathsf{T}} u_h \le y_h^{\mathsf{T}} u_h\).

GENERIC / metriplectic (generic) realization and Jacobi bases

For total energy \(E(x)\) (\(e_E = \nabla_x E\)) and entropy \(S(x)\) (\(e_S = \nabla_x S\)), the canonical generic metriplectic drift (R_h = 0) evaluated by IPHSStructureSpec.canonical_drift and audited via IPHSStructureSpec.validate is:

\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = J_h(x)\,e_E + M_h(x)\,e_S + G_h u_h + N_h r_h, \]

subject to skew-symmetry, positive semidefiniteness, and mutual degeneracy:

\[ J_h^{\mathsf{T}} = -J_h, \qquad M_h = M_h^{\mathsf{T}} \succeq 0, \qquad J_h e_S = 0, \qquad M_h e_E = 0, \qquad e_S^{\mathsf{T}} M_h e_S \ge 0. \]

For an isolated reaction-free system (\(u_h = 0\), \(r_h = 0\)), energy is conserved (\(\frac{\mathrm{d}E}{\mathrm{d}t} = e_E^{\mathsf{T}} J_h e_E + e_E^{\mathsf{T}} M_h e_S = 0\)) and entropy increases monotonically (\(\frac{\mathrm{d}S}{\mathrm{d}t} = e_S^{\mathsf{T}} M_h e_S \ge 0\)). Note that RELIC lowers GENERIC/metriplectic tendencies through IPHSStructureSpec.canonical_drift and advance_reaction_network ([I]); no separate standalone metriplectic time-integrator class is exposed ([N]).

Skew-symmetry of \(J_h\) (carrying the Poisson operator \(L_h\)) does not imply the Jacobi identity. IPHSStructureSpec admits three executable poisson_operator bases audited against validation.iphs.jacobi_tolerance:

  1. "zero_field": \(L(x) = 0\) identically (canonical_zero_field); all live certified production processes use zero reversible Poisson fields.

  2. "constant_field": constant skew matrix \(L\) with \(\partial_l L_{ij} = 0\), so the Jacobi residual vanishes identically (constant_field_exact).

  3. "state_field": importable callable \(L(x)\) audited by autograd via poisson_jacobi_residual over declared poisson_domain state samples and at bound Level 5 runtime points (sampled_domain_jacobi_residual):

\[ R_{ijk}(x) = \sum_{l} \left( L_{il}\frac{\partial L_{jk}}{\partial x_l} + L_{jl}\frac{\partial L_{ki}}{\partial x_l} + L_{kl}\frac{\partial L_{ij}}{\partial x_l} \right). \]

Static matrix_snapshot tensors carry no derivative information and fail closed for state-dependent Jacobi claims ([N]).

Reaction networks, open-system routing, and port interconnection

advance_reaction_network (relic.computation.operators.iphs) and reaction_network_check (relic.validation.framework.rules.reaction_network) govern stoichiometric kinetics \(\dot{x}_{\mathrm{rxn}} = N_h r_h\) (\(N_h \in \mathbb{R}^{n_s \times n_r}\), \(r_h \in \mathbb{R}^{n_r}\)):

  • Independent vs absorbed reaction representation: Within one IPHSStructureSpec, reactions either appear explicitly as \(+N_h r_h\) (requiring \(e_H^{\mathsf{T}} N_h r_h = 0\) for total energy or \(\le 0\) for free energy) or are absorbed into the dissipative operator (\(N_h r_h = -R_h e_H\) in dissipative_ph or \(N_h r_h = M_h e_S\) in generic, omitting \(+N_h r_h\) so rates are never double-counted).

  • Closed stoichiometry and physical affinity power: Internal conservation requires \(C_h N_h = 0\) (and optional charge neutrality \(z_h^{\mathsf{T}} N_h = 0\)). With chemical potentials \(\mu\), reaction affinity \(\mathcal{A} = -N_h^{\mathsf{T}} \mu\) satisfies dissipative power non-negativity \(P_{\mathrm{rxn}} = \mathcal{A}^{\mathsf{T}} r_h \ge 0\); division by positive temperature \(\sigma_{\mathrm{rxn}} = \mathcal{A}^{\mathsf{T}} r_h / T\) yields entropy production only when an executable \(T > 0\) and thermodynamic closure are bound.

  • Open-system exchange and overflow routing: Open systems keep internal stoichiometry closed (\(C_h N_h = 0\)) and route external exchange separately as \(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = N_h r_h + q_{\mathrm{open}}\) with \(C_h q_{\mathrm{open}} = \dot{\ell}_{\mathrm{open}}\) typed via OpenSystemRoute ("port", "boundary_export", "managed_export", "diagnostic_residual", or "observation"). Any bounds-clipping residual \(r_{\mathrm{clip}} = (x + \Delta x) - \operatorname{clip}(x + \Delta x, x_{\min}, x_{\max})\) must declare a valid route in overflow_routing_check ("storage", "boundary_outflow", "managed_export", "diagnostic_residual", or "rejected_step").

  • Port matching vs runtime port power: port_matching_check (relic.validation.framework.rules.port_matching) verifies static port declarations (effort/flow units \([P] = [e][f]\), dimensions, orientations, and signed incidence balance \(\sum_i s_i w_i = 0\)). Skew interconnection \(C = -C^{\mathsf{T}}\) induces \(J_{\mathrm{port}} = G_h C G_h^{\mathsf{T}}\), and passive feedback \(u_{\mathrm{int}} = -D y_h\) (\(D \succeq 0\)) induces \(R_{\mathrm{port}} = G_h D G_h^{\mathsf{T}}\) in dissipative_ph only (never added directly to GENERIC \(M_h\)). Actual power balance \(P_a + P_b \le 0\) is a runtime evaluation (port_power_units_check / feedback_power_ledger), distinct from static wiring checks.

Equivalence certificates and live repository inventory

IPHSEquivalenceCertificate (relic.computation.operators.iphs_certificate, audited by equivalence_certificate_check in relic.validation.framework.rules.equivalence_certificate) is the sole owner of each process’s structural claim level (Level 0 through Level 5).

Across the live repository, 90 unique concrete scientific Functor classes (37 BiologicalProcessFunctor, 27 TransportMechanismFunctor, 14 PhysicalFieldFunctor, and 12 ScaleCouplingFunctor; 0 uncertified) carry 90 primary class certificates plus 2 secondary constructor-scoped (constructor_selection) runtime-point certificates, totaling 92 YAML certificates under relic/parameters/database/relic/:

Both strict certificates (Level 4 and Level 5) audit the continuous-time canonical drift at the pre-step runtime state and require a matching governed_execution witness from a committed FunctorBase.__call__ step (without a witness, IPHSEquivalenceCertificate reports process_bound_runtime_unavailable).
